summary_of_runs.a_referee_model: refrun.py drives doc/recipes/prt.lua referee (port 8297/8299) with the honest player (prt.lua honest, forked servers, or stored machines in an epoch directory on the XFS reflink mount) and 1-4 black-box opponents from prt-dishonest.lua (quitter, tamperer, fabulist, forger) with random epoch-input and mcycle/leaf offsets (0, 1, 2..2000, 2000..200000), random join position of the honest player, and 0-5 random inputs per epoch. Two templates: the doc/recipes rolling calculator (calc expressions, rejections, bc errors, empty input, raw garbage that is not an EvmAdvance, inputs a few bytes over the 2 MiB rx buffer, ABI input of rx-size minus 28 bytes, raw rx-size+1) and the harness bare-metal template emit-output.bin (random small/medium payloads, R reject, H halt, E exception, oversized). An independent oracle (oracle.lua, plain emulator API: replay of the accepted inputs only, rejected inputs discarded, no-op deliveries skipped) gives the expected final canonical state and last notice. Checks per case: a winner exists, its final state equals the oracle, the honest player posted a claim, the proved notice matches the oracle (calc), no traceback/error/anomaly in the honest or referee stderr, no early exit, no stall (900 s cap). Result: 41 completed cases (seeds 1-7, 9-11, 13-36, 40-45 and 1000; 7 with the stored honest player), 0 problems. Two calc cases with a 2 MiB all-digit payload (seeds 8 and 12) were aborted by me for cost before claims were posted, not as failures; one first attempt of seed 1000 failed from my harness (epoch directory not created).
summary_of_runs.b_chain: chainrun.sh runs doc/recipes/prt-demo.sh on a PRIVATE wrapped anvil (port 8647, recipe parameters, --prune-history 256) with the patched Dave build, through a private copy of prt-demo.lua with the player-restart hook (kill -9 of the honest player at random orchestration waits, relaunched by prt-supervise.sh from players/honest/), output on work/prt-runs/dynprt (removed after each run). After each run: chain-oracle.lua fetches the app's InputAdded inputs from the chain and replays them from the template, comparing with the last checkpoint final state; chain-diff.py replays every settled epoch in the doc/recipes referee model (honest + quitter) from the same initial state with the same input bytes and compares the referee-model winner's computation hash and final state with the CommitmentJoined commitment on Dave's root tournament and the next epoch's settled initialMachineStateHash (same geometry: 2^10 mcycles per leaf, heights 62/30). Runs: smoke seed 101 (3 kills, 3 relaunches, ORACLE_MATCH), smoke seed 102 (3 kills, ORACLE_MATCH, DIFF_OK on epochs 0-2: identical computation hashes and final states), smoke seed 103 with kills restricted to epochs >= 1 (3 kills in epochs 1 and 2, ORACLE_MATCH, DIFF_OK), story seed 201 (7 adversaries + sentinel, 3 kills that all landed in epoch 0 / before epoch 1's dispute; both calculator epochs settled on the honest commitment and the demo's own assertions held; the oracle/diff step did not run because I edited the running script and anvil was gone). No lost match, stall, honest-player crash or referee-model/Dave disagreement observed.

not_covered: Random kills of the honest player DURING a dispute (bisection, uarch tournament, leaf proof) in the story: my only story run spent its 3 kills in epoch 0; the RESTART_MIN_EPOCH variant was run only in smoke mode, which has no dispute. Dispute-time kills remain covered only by the recipe's fixed restart points, which I did not re-run.
No chain-diff (referee model vs Dave) on the story run, i.e. with adversaries on chain; diff was done only for honest-only smoke epochs.

Custom adversaries beyond the four prt-dishonest.lua roles: a co-holder of the honest mcycle claim posting fabricated uarch claims that end at the honest state, Sybil floods of many claims, adversaries racing honest responses, deliberately late joins, and adversaries that disconnect mid-match (the latter crashes the referee model, R3-VARREFMODEL-2).
Referee-model clocks: the referee model uses logical blocks gated on every player's advance_time, so wall-clock speed, response budgets and timeout windows were never stressed.
Large inputs on the calculator template: 2 MiB payloads that the guest actually processes were aborted for cost; the honest player's claim cost on such inputs (R12) was not measured.
Output acceptance for non-notice outputs (bare-metal template): the referee model narrates only Notice outputs, so for those cases I checked only the winner's final state, not the outputs accepted.
Epochs with more than 5 inputs, the per-epoch input limit, and inputs at the 2^24 boundary (R1-A2-1 territory).
The released Dave constants (only the patched build with the recipe geometry was run on chain), PRT_TEST_REORG, sentinel drills, and real gas limits.
Stored honest player restarts inside the referee model (impossible without crashing the referee on disconnect).
Total compute exceeded the ~20 minute guideline because of the shared machine load (load average 15-21 during the runs); I stopped after 41 referee-model cases and 4 chain runs.
